subject: Black bands when trying to label x and y axis

messages.author: a9413cb4eedc9e12
messages.subject: Black bands when trying to label x and y axis
parts:
I seem to be getting something very strange. Weird black bands are appearing on the x and y axes when i use scale_x_discrete() & scale_y_discrete.  Please see the attached png file for the results. Am I in conflict with an earlier command, misunderstand the use of the scale commands  or do I have a serious problem?

Code and sessionInfo below.

Thanks

library(ggplot2)
dat1  <-  structure(list(label = c("iː", "eː", "æː", "äː", "oː",
"uː", "ɪ", "ɛ", "ɐ", "ɔ", "ʊ"), x = c(250L, 450L, 750L,
900L, 550L, 300L, 400L, 550L, 750L, 600L, 450L), y1 = c(2400L,
2100L, 1600L, 1200L, 800L, 600L, 1900L, 1700L, 1300L, 1100L,
900L), y2 = c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L)), .Names = c("label",
"x", "y1", "y2"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -11L
))

p  <-  ggplot(dat1, aes(x, y1, colour = (factor(y2))))
p  <-  p + geom_text(aes(label = label)) +  theme_bw() 
p  <-  p + scale_colour_discrete(name = "Languages",
             breaks = c(1,2),
             labels = c("babel", "gibberish"))
p         # works fine
             

p + scale_x_discrete("My x label") +   # What is this?
   scale_y_discrete("My y label")

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Black bands when trying to label x and y axis
parts:
On Wed, Jun 26, 2013 at 3:34 PM, John Kane <jrkr...@gmail.com> wrote:
p + scale_x_discrete("My x label") +   # What is this?
   scale_y_discrete("My y label")

I can confirm that this happens on my system too. It appears to be due to the fact that you are forcing a discrete scale onto integer data. 

If you use labs() it doesn't happen because it keeps the scale continuous. 

 p+ labs(x="My X Label", y= "My Y Label")

Brandon

messages.author: a9413cb4eedc9e12
messages.subject: Re: Black bands when trying to label x and y axis
parts:
On Wednesday, June 26, 2013 11:19:13 AM UTC-4, Brandon Hurr wrote:

On Wed, Jun 26, 2013 at 3:34 PM, John Kane <jrkr...@gmail.com> wrote:
p + scale_x_discrete("My x label") +   # What is this?
   scale_y_discrete("My y label")

I can confirm that this happens on my system too. It appears to be due to the fact that you are forcing a discrete scale onto integer data. 

If you use labs() it doesn't happen because it keeps the scale continuous. 

 p+ labs(x="My X Label", y= "My Y Label")

Brandon

That got it.  For some reason, probably a typo I was having a problem with xlab & ylab and decided to use the scales approach.  For some reason since I was using the scale_colour_discrete I got it into my head that I needed to use discrete here too.

Thanks very much
